study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Fetal Medicine Foundation algorithm risk for preeclampsia (based on maternal risk factors, mean arterial pressure, uterine arteries pulsatility index, placental growth factor, and soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1)
reason for induction of labor (premature rupture of membranes, postterm pregnancy, preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction, preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction)
outcome: intrapartum fetal compromise requiring cesarean delivery
urgent cesarean delivery for fetal compromise, failure to progress, or other reasons
cohort: The study included 12,249 women with singleton pregnancies who underwent induction of labor after routine assessments at 35 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks of gestation at King's College Hospital, London.
finding: The risk of cesarean delivery for intrapartum fetal compromise following induction of labor significantly increased with a higher Fetal Medicine Foundation 36-week preeclampsia risk, advancing gestational age, and nulliparity.
mod_finding: The Fetal Medicine Foundation 36-week preeclampsia risk model is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery for fetal compromise following induction of labor.
cross-section timing: Routine assessments for preeclampsia risk were performed at 35 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: Gestational age at assessment was 35 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks; gestational age at delivery ranged from <=37 weeks to >41 weeks, with findings specifically noting increases in risk from 35-42 weeks.
